prior_failure: II-G INSERT OR REPLACE produced duplicate name rows without conflict; preserve HOLD as independent historical observation. No reinterpretation of II-G.

experiment.arms: History absent/present x sequence target 0/7, each freshly created disk database
experiment.initialization: AUTOINCREMENT events table; optional prior INSERT then DELETE all rows; close CLI process after every SQL statement
experiment.treatment: Measure sqlite_sequence before treatment. If no matching row, INSERT INTO sqlite_sequence(name,seq) VALUES('events',t). If exactly one matching row, UPDATE sqlite_sequence SET seq=t WHERE name='events'. If more than one matching row, INVALID; no Y inspection.
experiment.treatment_fidelity: Verify exactly one sqlite_sequence row for name='events' and seq=t immediately after treatment, AND full visible schema/events table and public gate unchanged before future SQL
experiment.future_intervention: INSERT INTO events(note) VALUES ('probe') RETURNING id in new sqlite3 CLI process
experiment.prediction: For each equalized t, both histories produce the same id=t+1; across target sequences 0 and 7, future IDs differ
experiment.adjudication: Compare entire current W and H within corresponding targets, revalidate SQL process boundaries, treatment selection, all raw observations, expected and cross-arm future outputs
experiment.claim_ceiling: Strong local intervention-based sufficiency evidence for a specific SQLite internal allocator coordinate, contingent on successful treatment delivery, not a universal ontology theorem nor full future equivalence.
